subject: Post-demo: throughput & deployment trade-offs for OakBridge
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@oakbridge.ai>, Maya Patel <maya@oakbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + sizing worksheet (OakBridge)

Thanks for taking the demo today — quick recap and a set of follow-ups so we can lock the right deployment pathway. Attaching a worksheet and a small traffic sample we discussed.

Summary from the call:
- Primary goal: real-time enrichment for search & suggestions with sub-200ms P95 targets for the core route; secondary batch job for analytics.
- Candidate deployment modes: Hosted API (fast start), Dedicated reserved pool (predictable throughput), Private VPC (required for sensitive logs).
- Questions we flagged: sustained TPS, peak TPS, token distribution, latency SLOs, and whether you need on-prem for compliance.

Immediate asks (can you confirm by Thu?):
1) Sustained TPS and peak TPS (per endpoint) — we need 1-minute and 5-minute peaks if possible.
2) Token mix: what fraction are short requests (~8-64 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens)?
3) Any strict region or VPC requirements for the POC?
4) Sample payloads (attached traffic_sample.csv looks helpful).

Our initial thinking (to frame the options):
- If you need <200ms P95 and heavy short-token traffic, H100-backed dedicated nodes give best headroom.
- For cost-sensitive high-throughput with mixed tokens, A100-80GB reserved pool with quantized model variants can be a good tradeoff.
- We can offer a hybrid approach: start Dedicated reserved pool in our US cluster, and move to Private VPC for production if you need data residency.

Next steps: once we get the numbers above we’ll run a quick back-of-envelope GPU sizing and propose a 2-hour technical workshop (SE + infra) to show baseline config and trade-offs.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-worksheet-v1.xlsx, oakbridge_traffic_sample.csv

—
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@oakbridge.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@oakbridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + sizing worksheet (OakBridge)

Thanks Chloe — great demo. Quick answers and a small clarifying note.

Numbers:
- Sustained TPS (core suggestion endpoint): ~200 TPS sustained over 1 hour during business hours.
- Peak TPS: observed spikes up to 420 TPS for short bursts (30–60s) when marketing campaigns push traffic.
- Token mix: ~72% short requests (median ~34 tokens), ~22% medium (128–256 tokens), ~6% long tail (512–1024 tokens) used by our analytics pipeline.
- Latency SLO: our product team wants P95 <200ms initially; for the critical suggestions route they’d prefer <120ms.

Compliance: production must run inside a VPC with customer-managed KMS; for the POC we can start on a Dedicated reserved pool hosted in your US region if that expedites benchmarking. We’d like an on-prem option evaluated later in the quarter.

We attached a sanitized traffic dump (oakbridge_traffic_sample.csv). Also curious about cold-start behavior and how KV cache helps our short request tail.

Simon
Simon Lewis
Head of ML, OakBridge AI
simon.lewis@oakbridge.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@oakbridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + sizing worksheet (OakBridge)

Appreciate the details, Simon — that’s helpful. My read and an initial sizing sketch below. Attaching a short recommendation PDF.

Assumptions from Simon’s traffic sample: 72% short requests, majority under 50 tokens, 420 TPS short spikes. Core SLO target: aim for P95 <=120ms for the critical route (ambitious but achievable with the right hardware and caching).

Recommended POC config (fast path):
- Dedicated reserved pool (US cluster) to start — reduces variability and lets us instrument tail latencies.
- GPU choice: H100 nodes for the latency-sensitive route (single-model hot path). Expect roughly 300–380 short-request TPS per H100 under 8 concurrent streams with aggressive KV-prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Cost-optimized option: A100-80GB quantized variant. Expect ~180–240 short-request TPS per GPU but ~30–40% lower cost. Good for less latency-sensitive batch flows.
- Concurrency guidance: plan for 6–10 inference streams per GPU for the hot path; higher concurrency increases throughput but may push P95 up if response tokens are long.
- Tokenization & batching: enable continuous batching for medium/long tokens and prefix KV caching for repeat contexts — this should cut effective compute for short requests by ~20–35% depending on cache hit rate.

Operational asks for sizing refinement:
1) Can OakBridge share a 1-week real traffic percentile breakdown (1m, 5m peaks)?
2) Any endpoints that must absolutely be <120ms vs those that are OK at <200ms?
3) Are you comfortable with Dedicated-hosted for POC given VPC requirement for production later?

I’ll model two slab options (H100-first and A100-cost-optimized) and send a short spreadsheet that maps GPUs -> expected sustained TPS and estimated monthly compute cost. Proposed workshop: Thu Jul 22, 10am PT (SE-led).

Attachments: redwood-config-recommendation.pdf

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks Simon & Ben — good alignment. Simon, we can start the POC on a Dedicated reserved pool in our US cluster while we parallel the VPC evaluation. The workshop on Jul 22 works for our SE/infra team — I’ve penciled it in.

Action items I’ll own:
- Ben to send the GPU->TPS spreadsheet and two configuration slabs by EOD Mon (Jul 19).
- OakBridge to share the 1-week percentile breakdown and confirm which endpoints require <120ms.
- Marissa (CC) will prepare a simple procurement checklist and trial contract for a reserved pool POC.

If all looks good we’ll provision a small reserved pool (1–2 GPUs) for the workshop so we can run live profiling with your sample.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.
